root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer triple n, k, l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the quotient of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient indexed by k and the one indexed by l is actually a polynomial in q, then every coefficient of that polynomial is nonnegative.
quantifier_order: for all integers n, k, l
assume 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n
if the ratio of the two q-binomial coefficients is a polynomial in q
then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients

payload.theorem_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix an arbitrary triple (n,k,ℓ) under the theorem’s hypotheses. First replace k and ℓ by k' = min(k,n-k) and ℓ' = min(ℓ,n-ℓ); by Gaussian symmetry this does not change the quotient, and the assumption that the quotient is a polynomial forces ℓ' ≤ k' ≤ n/2. Next rewrite the reduced quotient as the balanced four-term q-factorial ratio ((q;q)_{ℓ'} (q;q)_{n-ℓ'}) / ((q;q)_{k'} (q;q)_{n-k'}). Cyclotomic factorization converts the polynomiality assumption into the family of floor inequalities required by the balanced q-factorial-ratio positivity theorem. Applying that bottleneck theorem yields coefficientwise nonnegativity for the reduced quotient, and therefore also for the original quotient.

steps.derives: Fix arbitrary integers n,k,ℓ with 0 ≤ k,ℓ ≤ n, and assume that Q(q) := [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the standard setup for proving a universally quantified implication: fix an arbitrary triple satisfying the hypotheses and name the quotient Q(q).

steps.derives: Define k' := min(k,n-k) and ℓ' := min(ℓ,n-ℓ).
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct definition of the reduced indices.

steps.derives: Q(q) = [n choose k']_q / [n choose ℓ']_q as a rational function in q.
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L1 states exactly that replacing each index by its minimum with its complement leaves the quotient unchanged.

steps.derives: The reduced indices satisfy 0 ≤ ℓ' ≤ k' ≤ ⌊n/2⌋.
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L2 gives deg([n choose r]_q)=r(n-r), and the degree function r(n-r) is weakly increasing on 0 ≤ r ≤ n/2. Since the quotient Q(q) is assumed polynomial in A0, its degree is nonnegative, so the degree of [n choose k']_q is at least the degree of [n choose ℓ']_q. Therefore ℓ' ≤ k'; by definition of k' and ℓ', both also lie in [0,⌊n/2⌋].

steps.derives: Set a := ℓ', b := n-ℓ', c := k', and d := n-k'. Then a+b=c+d=n and a ≤ c ≤ d ≤ b.
steps.trivial_justification: From A3, ℓ' ≤ k' ≤ n/2. Hence a=ℓ' ≤ c=k', and c=k' ≤ n-k'=d. Also d=n-k' ≤ n-ℓ'=b. Finally a+b=ℓ'+(n-ℓ')=n=k'+(n-k')=c+d.

By A2, Q(q) equals [n choose k']_q / [n choose ℓ']_q. The inequalities in A3 allow Lemma L3 to be applied to the triple (n,k',ℓ'). Lemma L3 rewrites this quotient as ((q;q)_{ℓ'} (q;q)_{n-ℓ'}) / ((q;q)_{k'} (q;q)_{n-k'}), which is exactly the displayed expression after substituting the definitions from A4.

steps.derives: For every positive integer m, one has ⌊a/m⌋ + ⌊b/m⌋ - ⌊c/m⌋ - ⌊d/m⌋ ≥ 0.
steps.trivial_justification: From A0 and A2, the reduced quotient [n choose k']_q / [n choose ℓ']_q is itself a polynomial in q. Lemma L4 applies to the ordered triple (n,k',ℓ') from A3, and therefore says that for every positive integer m the cyclotomic exponent ⌊ℓ'/m⌋ + ⌊(n-ℓ')/m⌋ - ⌊k'/m⌋ - ⌊(n-k')/m⌋ is nonnegative. Using the substitutions a=ℓ', b=n-ℓ', c=k', d=n-k' from A4 gives exactly the displayed inequalities.

steps.derives: Q(q) is a polynomial whose coefficients are all nonnegative integers.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A4 gives the balancing and ordering hypotheses a+b=c+d and a ≤ c ≤ d ≤ b. Step A6 gives the required floor inequalities for every positive integer m. Therefore Lemma L5 applies to the four-term q-factorial ratio F(q)=((q;q)_a (q;q)_b)/((q;q)_c (q;q)_d). Lemma L5 concludes that F(q) lies in Z[q] and has only nonnegative coefficients. By A5, Q(q)=F(q), so Q(q) has only nonnegative coefficients.

steps.derives: For all integers n,k,ℓ with 0 ≤ k,ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then every coefficient of that polynomial is nonnegative.
steps.trivial_justification: The triple (n,k,ℓ) in A0 was arbitrary subject to the theorem’s hypotheses, and A7 proves the desired coefficientwise nonnegativity for the corresponding quotient Q(q). Universal generalization therefore yields exactly the root theorem statement.

lemmas.statement_nl: For every integer n ≥ 0 and every integer r with 0 ≤ r ≤ n, define (q;q)_m := ∏_{i=1}^m (1-q^i) for m ≥ 1 and (q;q)_0 := 1, and define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}). Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q. Consequently, for any integers n,k,ℓ with 0 ≤ k,ℓ ≤ n, if k' := min(k,n-k) and ℓ' := min(ℓ,n-ℓ), then [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q = [n choose k']_q / [n choose ℓ']_q as rational functions in q.

Then [n choose r]_q is a polynomial of degree r(n-r). Hence, if integers n,k,ℓ satisfy 0 ≤ k,ℓ ≤ n and the quotient [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then with k' := min(k,n-k) and ℓ' := min(ℓ,n-ℓ) one has 0 ≤ ℓ' ≤ k' ≤ ⌊n/2⌋.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For 0 ≤ ℓ ≤ k ≤ n, the Gaussian quotient equals the balanced q-factorial ratio ((q;q)_ℓ (q;q)_{n-ℓ}) / ((q;q)_k (q;q)_{n-k}), equivalently the interval product ∏_{i=1}^{k-ℓ}(1-q^{n-k+i})/(1-q^{ℓ+i}).
quantifier_order: for all integers n,ℓ,k with 0 ≤ ℓ ≤ k ≤ n

lemmas.statement_nl:
For integers n,ℓ,k with 0 ≤ ℓ ≤ k ≤ n, define (q;q)_m := ∏_{j=1}^m (1-q^j) for m ≥ 1 and (q;q)_0 := 1, and define [n choose r]_q := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}). Then one has the exact identity
[n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q = ((q;q)_ℓ (q;q)_{n-ℓ}) / ((q;q)_k (q;q)_{n-k}) = ∏_{i=1}^{k-ℓ} (1-q^{n-k+i}) / (1-q^{ℓ+i}),
with the convention that an empty product equals 1.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: This is a direct algebraic identity obtained from the q-factorial formula for Gaussian coefficients.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Translates the hypothesis that the reduced quotient is a polynomial into a family of explicit floor inequalities.
lemmas.self_check_notes: The statement defines R_{n,k,ℓ} and Φ_d(q) locally and is independently understandable.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: The cyclotomic exponent of Φ_d(q) in R_{n,k,ℓ}(q)=((q;q)_ℓ (q;q)_{n-ℓ})/((q;q)_k (q;q)_{n-k}) is ⌊ℓ/d⌋+⌊(n-ℓ)/d⌋-⌊k/d⌋-⌊(n-k)/d⌋. Hence polynomiality of R_{n,k,ℓ}(q) is equivalent to nonnegativity of these floor differences for every d.
quantifier_order: for all integers n,ℓ,k with 0 ≤ ℓ ≤ k ≤ n

lemmas.statement_nl:
For integers n,ℓ,k with 0 ≤ ℓ ≤ k ≤ n, define (q;q)_m := ∏_{j=1}^m (1-q^j) for m ≥ 1 and (q;q)_0 := 1, define R_{n,k,ℓ}(q) := ((q;q)_ℓ (q;q)_{n-ℓ}) / ((q;q)_k (q;q)_{n-k}), and for each positive integer d let Φ_d(q) denote the d-th cyclotomic polynomial, characterized by 1-q^m = ∏_{d|m} Φ_d(q). Then the exponent of Φ_d(q) in the factorization of R_{n,k,ℓ}(q) over Q[q] is
⌊ℓ/d⌋ + ⌊(n-ℓ)/d⌋ - ⌊k/d⌋ - ⌊(n-k)/d⌋.
In particular, R_{n,k,ℓ}(q) is a polynomial in q if and only if this integer is nonnegative for every positive integer d.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: It concerns only cyclotomic factor bookkeeping and does not yet address coefficient signs.

lemmas.bottleneck_reason: After setting n=a+b, ℓ=a, and k=c, this is essentially the ordered balanced reformulation of the target theorem. It contains the genuine frontier step: turning the floor-inequality / polynomiality condition into coefficientwise nonnegativity.
lemmas.role_in_assembly: This is the main positivity engine for balanced four-term q-factorial ratios once the floor inequalities are known.
lemmas.self_check_notes: The statement is fully self-contained and explicitly marked as the bottleneck general theorem.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Under the balanced-order and floor-inequality assumptions, the four-term q-factorial ratio F(q)=((q;q)_a (q;q)_b)/((q;q)_c (q;q)_d) is a polynomial with all coefficients nonnegative.
quantifier_order: assume a+b=c+d and a ≤ c ≤ d ≤ b
assume for every positive integer m the displayed floor inequality

lemmas.statement_nl:
Let a,b,c,d be nonnegative integers with a+b=c+d and a ≤ c ≤ d ≤ b. Define (q;q)_m := ∏_{j=1}^m (1-q^j) for m ≥ 1 and (q;q)_0 := 1, and define
F(q) := ((q;q)_a (q;q)_b) / ((q;q)_c (q;q)_d).
Assume that for every positive integer m one has
⌊a/m⌋ + ⌊b/m⌋ - ⌊c/m⌋ - ⌊d/m⌋ ≥ 0.
Then F(q) belongs to Z[q], and every coefficient of F(q) is a nonnegative integer.
